analysis:
This batch holds only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/deadline-admission-estimators.md, head lines 1-6) and edits to docs/architecture/inference.md (head ranges ~632-638, ~882-918, ~1780). No executable code was supplied. The doc changes describe provider-side TTFT deadline admission estimator changes: per-batch-step decode pricing, MTP depth-gate mirroring, an isolated-prefill rate floor of 1/8 of the startup calibration idle rate, a 30-minute staleness rule for idle engines, newest-observation anchoring of measurement age, and the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES=0 rollback switch forwarded by `darkbloom start`.

Security relevance is limited to availability and admission fairness (TB-002, TB-007, ADV-002 and ADV-001 as a potential latency-manipulation adversary). The documented design keeps the actual deadline expiry, queue/cache projection and physical KV admission in force, and reviewed deadline-calibration requests keep their qualified per-row charge. There is no change to encryption, attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011), the prefix cache (T-041) or key custody. The environment variable is a rollback toggle only. It could be set by a local operator, who is already a trusted-for-availability party on their own machine and is not a new capability.

I cannot assess the implementation in AdmissionRateEstimators.swift, which was not supplied. Questions for integration: whether the 1/8 floor and the 30-minute staleness rule could let a provider underprice or over-admit work (an availability or SLA concern, not a confidentiality one), and whether the out-of-order observation handling in EnginePerformanceMeasurements.Rate is correct. No finding is raised because the docs alone do not show a concrete regression.
